Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3707; invisible:--invisible (thing).
BiblicalUsage: The invisible things of God, the unseen God, the King eternal, immortal, invisible. Paul says the invisible things of God are clearly seen by the things that are made, the Son is the image of the invisible God, and Moses endured as seeing Him who is invisible. The word names what the eye cannot see and faith must take hold of.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the invisible is more real than the visible: the God no eye has seen made the world every eye sees, and Moses endured by seeing Him who is invisible. I hold that faith is not believing in nothing but seeing what is truly there, and the invisible God is the most solid thing I know.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
